This reference layer helps teachers reuse design and fabrication learning without pretending that every technology course is Manufacturing. A method such as vector drawing, laser cutting, 3D printing, sewing, CNC machining, or hand fabrication becomes meaningful only when students apply it to the users, materials, systems, use boundaries, and quality criteria of a technology area.

::: {.ter-transfer-statement}
The fabrication method is transferable. The application changes with the technology area.
:::

These pages are **not another numbered curriculum unit**. Enter here when you already know the technology context; use the [curriculum pathway](../index.qmd) when you want a sequence organized by design and fabrication method.

## Four project families that transfer well

<div class="ter-family-grid">
<article class="ter-family-card"><h3>Organizer</h3><p>The same retention-and-access problem becomes a socket rack in TTJ, a cable module in TEJ, a sanitized-tool workflow model in TXJ, or a labelled supply organizer in TPJ. Students measure the actual objects and test reach, visibility, stability, and cleaning access.</p></article>
<article class="ter-family-card"><h3>Display</h3><p>A stable display can communicate a brand in TGJ, plant information in THJ, a menu in TFJ, a building detail in TCJ, or a public-health message in TPJ. The audience, viewing distance, accessibility, and environment change the criteria.</p></article>
<article class="ter-family-card"><h3>Gauge or template</h3><p>A reference tool may check hole spacing in TMJ, screw length in TCJ, wiring pitch in TEJ, service part size in TTJ, or repeatable label placement in TGJ. It must state exactly what it measures and its limits.</p></article>
<article class="ter-family-card"><h3>Portable work module</h3><p>A bounded module makes a complete task visible and movable: electronics test leads, styling consultation materials, field-observation tools, construction layout tools, or event-service information. Handles, centre of mass, inventory, and setup sequence become design evidence.</p></article>
</div>

## Use the reference layer responsibly

Each project card names a problem, course context, process, skills, scale, material, structural concern, use boundary, library starting point, lesson link, and extension. These boundaries describe what a classroom prototype is and is not intended to do; they are not machine operating instructions. Treat dimensions as hypotheses until students measure the real object and environment. Course codes identify useful contexts, not official expectation mappings; teachers should connect a chosen project to their current curriculum document and local board requirements.

Machine-specific safety instruction, operating procedures, assessments, and authorization are kept outside this public website. Follow your school board's safety guidelines and the course-specific instruction provided by your teacher. Students in Mr. Andrade's classes can find that information in Google Classroom.
